children.text: Model a neutral air molecule as a fixed point charge +q inside a uniform spherical negative cloud of total charge −q,mass m,radius r. Its small natural vibration frequency is ω0. Light drives E=E0cosωt ŷ and cloud displacement y=y0cosωt. Use the negative charge sign in its force. For low-frequency radiation assume ω≪ω0. Mean optical intensity is I=cε0E0²/2. Molecule number density is n0 and scattered power per molecule is s. For numerical estimates take q=e=\(1.602\times10^{-19}\) C,m=me=\(9.109\times10^{-31}\) kg,ε0=\(8.854\times10^{-12}\) SI,c=\(3.0\times10^{8}\) m/s,n0=\(2.54\times10^{25}\) m⁻³,ω0=\(1.25\times10^{16}\) rad/s and ω=\(3.25\times10^{15}\) rad/s. Darjeeling is h=2042 m above sea level. Everest has height H=8848 m,distance d=170 km, and Kanchenjunga has H=8586 m,d=75 km. Earth radius is R=6378 km. Ignore refraction and variation of molecular density with altitude. For the source's intensity comparison use equal effective source luminosities and geometric dilution I∝d⁻², plus exponential atmospheric attenuation. The unpolluted Kanchenjunga intensity at Darjeeling defines the fixed reference. A peak is visible if its intensity is at least 5% of this reference.
Write the equation of motion for y.
Find the forced sinusoidal solution and amplitude.
Find the time-dependent dipole for ω≪ω0.
Use dimensional analysis to find how mean radiated power depends on p0,ε0,c,ω, up to a dimensionless constant.
Take the dimensionless constant as 1/(12π). Express s using E0,ω0,ω and the molecular parameters.
Write the differential equation for I(x).
Solve with I(0)=I0 and find L.

With that uniform pollution, find the intensity of each mountain relative to the original fixed reference. Which peaks remain visible?

children.text: The restoring acceleration is −ω0²y and the electric force is −qE. Hence \(\ddot y+\omega_0^2y=-(qE_0/m)\cos\omega t\).

Substitute y=y0cosωt to obtain \(y_0=qE_0/[m(\omega^2-\omega_0^2)]\). This signed coefficient is negative below resonance. The nonnegative amplitude is its absolute value. The steady particular solution excludes free oscillations and resonance.

The dipole vector points from negative to positive charge, so \(\mathbf p=-qy\hat y\simeq[q^2E_0/(m\omega_0^2)]\cos\omega t\hat y\). Its oscillation amplitude is q²E0/(mω0²), and its instantaneous magnitude takes the absolute value of the cosine. This distinguishes the signed sinusoid from the nonnegative magnitude.
Inside the uniform cloud the field grows linearly with displacement. Action and reaction give restoring force \(-q^2y/(4\pi\epsilon_0r^3)\). Therefore \(\omega_0=q/\sqrt{4\pi\epsilon_0mr^3}\).
Matching dimensions in s=kp0αωβε0γcδ gives α=2,β=4,γ=−1,δ=−3. Thus \(s=k p_0^2\omega^4/(\epsilon_0c^3)\).
Balance power in a slab of area A and thickness dx: I(x)A−I(x+dx)A=n0sA dx. Hence \(dI/dx=-n_0s\). Since s∝E0²∝I this is dI/dx=−I/L.
Combine B2 with I=cε0E0²/2 to obtain \[L=\frac{6\pi\epsilon_0^2m^2c^4}{n_0q^4}\left(\frac{\omega_0}{\omega}\right)^4,\qquad I(x)=I_0e^{-x/L}.\]
Substitution of the supplied molecular and optical data gives approximately L=130 km. The source uses rounded constants and a ten-percent numerical acceptance range.

Let θ=d/R. In the source projection construction the local horizontal through the observer intersects the mountain radius at radius (R+h)secθ. Similar triangles give \[H^{\prime}=R+h-\frac{(R+h)^2}{R+H}\sec(d/R).\] To leading order in h/R,H/R,d/R, \(H^{\prime}\simeq H-h-d^2/(2R)\). The full source construction gives approximately 6096 m for Kanchenjunga and 4534 m for Everest. Both extend above the local horizontal. Show Earth centre, observer radius, mountain radius and the observer's tangent line.

For equal effective luminosities, \[\frac{I_E}{I_K}=\left(\frac{75}{170}\right)^2e^{-(170-75)/130}\simeq0.093.\] The distances and L must use the same units. This exceeds 0.05, so Everest is visible in this model.
\(L_p=1/(8n\pi r^2)\). Each particle has mass 4πr³ρ/3, so n=ρp/(4πr³ρ/3), giving \(L_p=r\rho/(6\rho_p)\). Convert ρp=\(5\times10^{-9}\) kg/m³ and ρ=3000 kg/m³ to obtain Lp=50 km.

The total attenuation has exponent −d/L−d/Lp. Thus \(I_K/I_{ref}=e^{-75/50}\simeq0.223\), while \(I_E/I_{ref}=0.093e^{-170/50}\simeq0.0031\). Kanchenjunga remains above 5%, while Everest does not. The reference remains the unpolluted Kanchenjunga intensity, rather than being reset after pollution.

solution.text:
Maxwell, Rayleigh and Mount Everest
a.1. Driven cloud equation
The restoring acceleration is −ω0²y and the electric force is −qE. Hence \(\ddot y+\omega_0^2y=-(qE_0/m)\cos\omega t\).
a.2. Oscillation amplitude
Substitute y=y0cosωt to obtain \(y_0=qE_0/[m(\omega^2-\omega_0^2)]\). This signed coefficient is negative below resonance. The nonnegative amplitude is its absolute value. The steady particular solution excludes free oscillations and resonance.
a.3. Induced dipole
The dipole vector points from negative to positive charge, so \(\mathbf p=-qy\hat y\simeq[q^2E_0/(m\omega_0^2)]\cos\omega t\hat y\). Its oscillation amplitude is q²E0/(mω0²), and its instantaneous magnitude takes the absolute value of the cosine. This distinguishes the signed sinusoid from the nonnegative magnitude.
a.4. Natural frequency
Inside the uniform cloud the field grows linearly with displacement. Action and reaction give restoring force \(-q^2y/(4\pi\epsilon_0r^3)\). Therefore \(\omega_0=q/\sqrt{4\pi\epsilon_0mr^3}\).
b.1. Radiated-power dimensions
Matching dimensions in s=kp0αωβε0γcδ gives α=2,β=4,γ=−1,δ=−3. Thus \(s=k p_0^2\omega^4/(\epsilon_0c^3)\).
b.2. Low-frequency radiated power
Use p0=q²E0/(mω0²): \[s=\frac{q^4E_0^2}{12\pi\epsilon_0m^2c^3}\left(\frac\omega{\omega_0}\right)^4.\]
c.1. Attenuation equation
Balance power in a slab of area A and thickness dx: I(x)A−I(x+dx)A=n0sA dx. Hence \(dI/dx=-n_0s\). Since s∝E0²∝I this is dI/dx=−I/L.
c.2. Attenuation length
Combine B2 with I=cε0E0²/2 to obtain \[L=\frac{6\pi\epsilon_0^2m^2c^4}{n_0q^4}\left(\frac{\omega_0}{\omega}\right)^4,\qquad I(x)=I_0e^{-x/L}.\]
c.3. Molecular attenuation estimate
Substitution of the supplied molecular and optical data gives approximately L=130 km. The source uses rounded constants and a ten-percent numerical acceptance range.
d.1. Visible mountain heights
Let θ=d/R. In the source projection construction the local horizontal through the observer intersects the mountain radius at radius (R+h)secθ. Similar triangles give \[H^{\prime}=R+h-\frac{(R+h)^2}{R+H}\sec(d/R).\] To leading order in h/R,H/R,d/R, \(H^{\prime}\simeq H-h-d^2/(2R)\). The full source construction gives approximately 6096 m for Kanchenjunga and 4534 m for Everest. Both extend above the local horizontal. Show Earth centre, observer radius, mountain radius and the observer's tangent line.
e.1. Unpolluted visibility ratio
For equal effective luminosities, \[\frac{I_E}{I_K}=\left(\frac{75}{170}\right)^2e^{-(170-75)/130}\simeq0.093.\] The distances and L must use the same units. This exceeds 0.05, so Everest is visible in this model.
f.1. Aerosol attenuation
\(L_p=1/(8n\pi r^2)\). Each particle has mass 4πr³ρ/3, so n=ρp/(4πr³ρ/3), giving \(L_p=r\rho/(6\rho_p)\). Convert ρp=\(5\times10^{-9}\) kg/m³ and ρ=3000 kg/m³ to obtain Lp=50 km.
g.1. Polluted visibility
The total attenuation has exponent −d/L−d/Lp. Thus \(I_K/I_{ref}=e^{-75/50}\simeq0.223\), while \(I_E/I_{ref}=0.093e^{-170/50}\simeq0.0031\). Kanchenjunga remains above 5%, while Everest does not. The reference remains the unpolluted Kanchenjunga intensity, rather than being reset after pollution.
